The tasks are category learning/dual-task paradigms rather than explicit problem-solving across domains. Furthermore, the full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables (Talairach/MNI) of task-related activation peaks required by I7. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and I7. No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered.

The study reports a task-based fMRI/EEG experiment in healthy adults (n=8) using a mental-arithmetic (continuous subtraction) task that involves goal-directed operations, sequencing, and rule-based computation consistent with problem-solving (I5). It includes whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM99 analyses with group-level one-sample t-tests across subjects (I6). BOLD (fMRI) analyses are reported (I8). Data were normalized to an MNI template and stereotactic coordinates are reported in the text (e.g., [−42, −10, 42]), with voxelwise results and thresholding described, satisfying the requirement for coordinate reporting (I7) and acceptable reporting formats (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no between-group-only contrasts, not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet the review objective for two main reasons: (1) I5 not met — the task is a Go/NoGo response inhibition paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based solution discovery). (2) I6 not met — participants are ages 8–20 (predominantly minors/adolescents); the meta-analysis requires whole-brain group effects in healthy adult individuals. The study does meet other technical criteria: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach/MNI), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based on I5 and I6 not being satisfied.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the behavioral paradigms (response-switching and visual-switching) examine task-set switching, response selection, and attentional control. Subjects are instructed which rules to apply and must switch between these instructed rules; they are not required to identify or discover solutions, to engage in open-ended problem formulation, or to perform goal-directed problem solving as defined in I5 (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Because the primary aim and tasks do not meet the review’s definition of problem-solving across domains, the study is excluded.

This study is a methods paper using real-time fMRI and SPRT, applied to face vs. house perception and simulations; it does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (I5 not met). The empirical real-data example is a single-subject/ROI-focused FFA analysis rather than a whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6 not met). The paper reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8 met). It appears analyses focus on an ROI (mask of 717 voxels) and comparisons within that ROI rather than whole-brain voxelwise, and results are presented as ROI maps rather than providing stereotactic coordinate tables for whole-brain group effects; thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Summary: Excluded because E3 applies; inclusion criteria met: I8; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9.

The study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving per the review definition (I5). The task involves passive viewing of videos with button presses to indicate change points (event parsing/attention), not goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to find solutions. The paper does meet other relevant inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/maps reported in figures). However, the manuscript does not present stereotactic coordinates in the provided full text, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., ROI-only, between-group-only, non-empirical). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing key inclusion criteria (primarily I5; also I7 not satisfied based on provided text).

The study uses task-based fMRI (movie watching) but does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing rule-based solutions). It reports developmental (child vs adult) group comparisons and modularity analyses but does not report task-related activation foci in stereotactic coordinates for a problem-solving contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm) and I7 (no task-related stereotactic coordinate activation results reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (study presents group comparisons and does not provide healthy-group task effect/contrast relevant to problem-solving). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This fMRI study in healthy adults examines sequencing of actions (script task) and sentence-word order, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI addressing sequencing/planning/problem-like processing), I6 (healthy adult participants with reported group-level whole-brain activation summaries), and I8 (BOLD fMRI results reported). However, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space or provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures (only Brodmann areas and ROI-based subject counts), so it fails I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) clearly apply; the study is not an ROI-only analysis in the methodological sense but lacks standardized coordinates. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to missing I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. This is a methodological fMRI study of a sparse-regression deconvolution method (SPFM) validated on simulated data and a visuomotor single-trial finger-tapping task in five healthy subjects. The fMRI paradigm assesses moral judgment (decision-making about hypothetical moral dilemmas), which does not clearly require goal-directed problem solving as defined (identifying/planning/sequencing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a solution). Criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level task fMRI including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, not purely between-group contrasts, empirical human data present). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study of semantic/word-association (post-lexical semantic relatedness judgments). It includes whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults, reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, and BOLD results. However, it does NOT meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the task is a semantic relatedness/lexical decision, not a goal-directed problem-solving activity involving planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of criterial classification and decision-rule effects during memory and perceptual classification tasks (forced-choice, same-different, independent-classification). While it meets neuroimaging methodological criteria (whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates, BOLD fMRI analyses), it does not examine 'problem solving' as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution or critical-thinking operations to generate/execute a solution strategy). Instead, the tasks are stimulus classification/judgment problems rather than planning or sequencing actions to solve a previously unknown problem. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based PET investigation of decision-making (exploration/exploitation) using a stochastic gambling task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-driven critical thinking/planning/sequencing within a rule framework to reach a correct or novel solution). Although it meets neuroimaging criteria (whole-brain group-level PET rCBF analyses reported with stereotactic coordinates), it does not examine problem-solving across domains. Full text appears complete.

The study includes a Tower of London planning task that meets the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing of moves to reach a target). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants, with images normalized to MNI space and lists of significant clusters (coordinate results) provided. Voxelwise SPM results are reported and available in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is mental rotation / perspective-taking, a visuospatial transformation task, but does not meet the review's defined "problem-solving" requirement involving planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 while satisfying other imaging-related criteria.

This PET study reports whole-brain, task-based imaging in healthy adults performing a stochastic reversal learning task that is goal-directed (maximize reward) and requires identification and adaptation of stimulus–outcome contingencies (i.e., evaluation, planning/adjustment of actions, and execution to obtain reward), which fits the provided definition of a problem-solving task. The study used group-level whole-brain rCBF analyses (SPM) in healthy adult participants, reported task-related rCBF results, and indicates voxelwise analyses with reported activation clusters (results presented via contrasts and correlation maps; figures/tables referenced). Thus it meets I5 (goal-directed adaptive problem-solving/reversal learning), I6 (group whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (voxelwise stereotactic results reported/available in figures/tables), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a methods paper applying a group network detection algorithm to fMRI data collected during a motor tracking/squeezing task, not a problem-solving task. Exclusion reasons: E3 (reports only ROI-based results). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (uses BOLD fMRI). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is motor tracking, not defined problem-solving as per review), I6 (does not perform a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis; uses anatomically defined ROIs), I7 (does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (fixed-effects across N=5), uses BOLD contrast maps in MNI space, and reports activation maps/tables, but the experimental task is a visual checkerboard with attentional modulation (attend/ignore/discriminate). It does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing or rule-based solution processes such as semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical tasks). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a non-empirical commentary/review (Exclusion E6). It does not report original task-based fMRI or PET experiment data in healthy adults: no methods, participant details, task design, group-level whole-brain analyses, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results are presented. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses reported), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating probabilistic prediction/uncertainty and learning, but it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring critical evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to arrive at a (previously unknown) solution). The task here involves predicting which of two figures will 'win' based on learned probabilities—this is decision-making/probabilistic learning rather than problem solving per the I5 definition. The paper meets whole-brain, group-level BOLD analysis requirements (I6, I8) but does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving paradigm). Also, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables/explicit coordinates in Talairach/MNI space in the text excerpt supplied, so I7 cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Outcome: EXCLUDE because I5 not met (and I7 unconfirmed).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study of contingency learning/reversal learning and executive control, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinate results in tables/figures), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the experimental task is a two-alternative choice/reversal-learning paradigm examining contingency detection, valuation, and updating (win-stay/lose-shift behavior and responses to value/effect changes), rather than a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning, critical evaluation, sequencing of actions to reach a novel solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failure to meet I5.

This study was excluded because it does not meet the review’s core problem-solving task requirement (I5). The fMRI task is a dual-task letter/number discrimination paradigm measuring executive function/dual-task processing (maintenance, coordination, response selection, conflict monitoring) rather than a problem-solving task entailing a goal, planning/sequencing operations, or deriving a previously unknown solution within a delimited rule set. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). I7 (stereotactic coordinates) likely reported in tables but are not explicit in the provided text; however, this uncertainty does not change exclusion because I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I5: the in-scanner task is a Go/No Go response-inhibition/attention task, which does not qualify as a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain fMRI with group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6). Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a theory-of-mind (ToM) moving-shapes paradigm assessing social cognition/mentalizing, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem identification, planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not involve problem-solving as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the review definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The modified rock–paper–scissors paradigm is an inhibition-of-stereotyped-response task (attempting to ‘lose’ vs. ‘win’) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution to arrive at a novel/appropriate solution as defined in I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an inhibitory response task, not a problem-solving task per the review definition). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore EXCLUDE due to failure to satisfy I5.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’ definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task used (POP, a Stroop-derived cognitive-control/conflict task) probes executive control/preparation and conflict monitoring rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a (previously unknown) solution. While the study includes whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with group-level effects in elderly healthy comparison participants (I6) and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), it does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in the main text or tables accessible here (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results in MNI space and provides coordinate tables; however, the experimental task is a delayed-encoding recognition/manipulation paradigm (chunking, segmenting, binding) testing working memory and sequencing of prelearned items rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed search for a solution or planning/executive problem solving to arrive at a novel or discovered solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Detailed summary: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not evaluate a problem-solving task as defined). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a whole‑brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting group-level BOLD effects and stereotactic coordinates (MNI), it does not investigate problem‑solving as defined in the review (I5). The tasks are social judgements (approachability and perceived intelligence from faces), involving binary evaluative decisions, not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule set to reach a solution. Therefore I5 is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This task-based fMRI study involves goal-directed decision-making and planning (e.g., deciding when to execute left turns with oncoming traffic under traffic rules and performing secondary cognitive tasks while driving), fulfilling the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (16 young drivers) using BOLD fMRI (I6,I8). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space and shown in tables/figures (I7,I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), contain healthy-group task effects, and are empirical. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the sugar production factory (SPF) paradigm, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (explicit goal, need to figure out actions to reach a target and adjust strategy across trials). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (inter-subject t-tests) with BOLD contrasts pre- and post-training and uses stereotactic atlases (Talairach Daemon/WFU_Pickatlas) to report anatomical loci; task-related activations and learning-related increases/decreases are described and implied to be reported in standardized coordinate space/tables/figures. ROI analyses are supplementary and the paper does not rely solely on ROI results. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and the study should be included.

This study uses an N-back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem formulation, planning/sequencing to derive a novel solution). While it does report whole-brain BOLD fMRI results in stereotactic (Talairach) space and includes healthy adult comparison subjects, it does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses with healthy adult participants), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory N-back, not problem solving). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment that examines semantic event sequencing—a sequencing/planning executive task consistent with the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning and sequencing). It reports whole-brain, group-level within-group effects for healthy adult controls and between-group contrasts, with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise BOLD results. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9. Full text content is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses an n-back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence the task required goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). It does meet other required criteria: I6 (includes healthy adult group-level whole-brain analyses and within-group task effects in controls), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results presented in figures and text). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because it does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults studying cognitive control, working memory, and target detection/switching, not a problem-solving task as defined in the review (no goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a solution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results indicated as available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met) and the neuroimaging analysis is ROI-based rather than a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (E3; I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI results), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/SVC results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task; task is emotional face perception/gender identification), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis; primary approach used predefined ROIs with small-volume corrections). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not address the meta-analysis objective and is excluded.

This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level rCBF analyses (SPM) in healthy adult participants using Talairach coordinates and presents voxelwise task-related effects across the brain. The tasks require subjects to learn and apply arbitrary stimulus–response mappings and to evaluate whether an outcome (arrow) matches the correct response, which constitutes goal-directed, rule-based problem-solving (evaluation, planning/selection, execution under rule constraints). Results (increases and decreases in rCBF) are reported stereotactically and in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met.

Full text is complete. The task is a numerical Stroop/number comparison (magnitude judgment with interference), which is a perceptual/cognitive comparison task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical thinking to arrive at a solution). Thus I5 is not met. The study does meet other inclusion criteria (I6: whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults; I7: stereotactic coordinates reported; I8: BOLD analysis reported; I9: voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study does not meet the core inclusion criterion I5: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined. Instead, it examines pragmatic language comprehension (metaphor and sarcasm) and mentalizing processes. It does meet other methodological inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates, e.g., left amygdala at −26,0,−20), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the paper must be excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). It is an fMRI investigation of spontaneous speech and syntactic complexity (language production) in schizophrenia and controls, not a task requiring problem solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem-solving). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses task-based BOLD fMRI and reports stereotactic coordinates/voxelwise results, but it does NOT study a problem-solving task and does NOT include healthy adult participants. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is cue-reactivity, not problem-solving), I6 (participants are alcohol-dependent patients, not healthy adults). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (does not include any healthy-group task effect). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the review because it fails the required population and task-type inclusion criteria.

This is a feedback-based paired-associate declarative memory study, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task involves learning arbitrary word pairs via feedback and recognition, not engaging critical thinking processes such as evaluating a problem, planning or sequencing actions to reach a novel solution. Thus inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not met. The study does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of decision-making (two-choice prediction/response tasks) in schizophrenia patients with healthy comparison subjects. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (contains whole-brain, group-level analyses that include healthy adult participants) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the experimental task is a decision-making/prediction paradigm and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a correct/novel solution) and thus does not address the target construct; I7 — the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the supplied content; I9 — while results are described, coordinate tables/figures/supplementary coordinate lists are not present in the provided text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not meet the key conceptual inclusion criterion I5 (and lacks explicit coordinate reporting in the provided text).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses and BOLD effects (I6, I8 met). However, the experimental paradigm is a verb-generation/semantic-selection task (generate a verb associated with a noun). This does not match the review’s definition of problem-solving (I5): it lacks a clear goal-oriented problem requiring planning/sequencing or execution of operations to reach a correct/novel solution; it is primarily semantic retrieval and selection. Additionally, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space in the excerpt (I7/I9 not demonstrated in the supplied content). Therefore the study does not meet the core inclusion criterion I5 and is excluded.

The full text is complete. The study uses whole-brain, task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, but it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a financial investment/decision-making paradigm (decide whether to invest additional money given costs and probabilities) focused on sunk-cost bias and value-based choice. It lacks elements required by I5 such as formulation of a goal that requires discovering or sequencing actions to reach a previously unknown solution, explicit planning/sequencing operations under rule sets to derive a correct solution, or performance of critical thinking processes to solve a defined problem. Therefore, despite satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9, it fails I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates planning and set-shifting using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task. The task requires subjects to identify classification rules, plan shifts in strategy, and execute rule-based responses—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in 10 healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates and figures for activation peaks (I7, I9), and uses BOLD contrast (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group comparison only, and is empirical).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The experimental tasks are visuomotor coordinate-transformation and mental-rotation/copying tasks (perceptual and executional visuomotor control), not a problem-solving task as defined (i.e., requiring goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level PET analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (stereotactic Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a modified Sternberg working memory (maintenance-retrieval) paradigm examining practice-related changes in short-term memory retrieval and automation, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem decomposition, planning/sequencing operations to find novel solutions). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study investigates simple comparative judgment tasks (selecting the larger number/size/luminance) rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning, sequencing, and executing operations to arrive at a novel or complex solution). Thus I5 is not met. The full text is complete and shows that the study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6); stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI (I7); BOLD fMRI analysis reported (I8); and voxelwise results available in text/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis because it does not examine a problem-solving task as specified (I5 not met).

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined). While the Iowa Gambling Task has a goal and involves learning/strategy, it is a decision-making/reward-processing paradigm rather than a problem-solving task involving evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions within a rule set to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

The study is an fMRI investigation of value-based decision making / learning (restless bandit) and does not test a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving explicit evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions within rule-based frameworks to arrive at a correct/novel solution). Although participants had a goal (maximize reward) and learned contingencies, the paradigm is best characterized as reinforcement learning/decision-making under uncertainty rather than problem solving (e.g., logical, semantic, algebraic, or rule-based problem-solving). The paper does meet other inclusion criteria (whole-brain group fMRI, reports MNI coordinates, BOLD analyses, and reports voxelwise results), but it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a simultaneous EEG-fMRI study using an n-back working-memory paradigm with two single subjects. While it reports BOLD analyses (I8) and provides whole-brain projection/thresholded maps (satisfying I9), it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (n-back is a working-memory task, not a domain-general problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing/deriving solutions), and it does not include a group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults (I6 is not met; only two single-subject analyses are presented). The paper also does not present stereotactic coordinate tables for group-level activations (I7 not satisfied). Accordingly, exclusion criterion E5 applies (the study does not include any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a methodological paper presenting an Information Bottleneck clustering approach for fMRI data and illustrative analyses on visual stimulation datasets. It does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving / critical thinking/planning/executing rule-based operations). While the paper reports stereotactic coordinates (I7), BOLD analyses (I8), and voxelwise results in figures/text (I9), it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task) or I6 (clear whole-brain group-level task effects in healthy adults representing a substantive group study). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates number line and brightness estimation (mapping magnitudes onto a spatial line). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults reporting Talairach coordinates, it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the experimental tasks are perceptual/estimation mappings rather than problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to derive a novel solution). Therefore it fails I5 and must be excluded. The full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This PET study uses the Montreal Card Sorting Task, which qualifies as a problem-solving/set-shifting task (I5). It reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7) and provides voxelwise peak results in the text (I9). However, the analysis is restricted to the striatum: the authors state that only peaks within the striatum were considered and statistical correction assumed a search volume equal to the striatum, indicating a region-limited (ROI) analysis rather than a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Additionally, the PET modality used here is a molecular D2-binding analysis ([11C]raclopride BP) and does not report BOLD or rCBF measures, so inclusion criterion I8 is not met. Finally, the study does not provide a whole-brain group-level analysis (I6 not met). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy adults that reports group-level voxelwise analyses (Talairach-transformed data) of a numerical comparison/size-congruity (number Stroop) task. However, the experimental task is a magnitude comparison (which-number-is-larger) and manipulation of stimulus congruity, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed multi-step planning, sequencing, or execution of operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control/oddball target detection embedded in sad vs. neutral contexts in unipolar depression. It does not examine a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing and executing operations to arrive at a novel or correct solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This is a task-based fMRI study that used the Paced Visual Serial Addition Test (PVSAT), a rule-based arithmetic/working-memory task (goal-directed addition operations), which fits the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (goal, rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions). The study includes healthy adult controls and reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD results. Coordinates and activation results are reported (main text and supplementary), satisfying the reportability criterion. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study does not meet the review’s primary scope of problem-solving tasks (Inclusion I5). The fMRI paradigm is a visual working memory (change-detection) task, which does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution generation as defined for the meta-analysis. In addition, the analytic approach focused on predefined regions-of-interest (replication within eight ROIs) rather than a whole-brain group-level analysis, so it does not satisfy the requirement for at least one whole-brain analysis (Inclusion I6 not met). The full text is available and includes methods, results, and discussion. The paper does meet several other technical criteria: stereotactic coordinates are reported (I7), BOLD analyses are reported (I8), and voxelwise/cluster results are provided in tables/figures (I9). Because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, the study must be excluded.

This study reports a task in which healthy adult participants learn and discover abstract stimulus–response rules via reinforcement (hierarchical rule discovery), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule discovery, planning/sequencing of actions, and execution within a rule framework). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses (1-sample t-tests, FWE-corrected), reports stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z) for activations, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Voxelwise results are presented in the main text/figures and ROI analyses supplement the whole-brain findings. Participants are healthy adults (subset of 16 of 20), and analyses examine task-related increases. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s core task definition of problem solving (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results indicated as available in figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI decoding study of finger movements (index vs. middle) in healthy adults using whole-brain voxelwise analyses and BOLD signals, but it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (goal-directed evaluation/planning/sequencing to reach a solution within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). The study reports a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task that requires goal-directed rule-based classification, planning/set-shifting and execution—meeting the review’s definition of problem solving. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.
